title: Spiked beer and limburger sandwich at the Spinning Wheel
summary: Stories of the Italian owner's spiked beer and a limburger and onion sandwich that upset his wife.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, sure. And everybody in the band would drink, you understand what I mean. There was an Italian fella running the Spinning Wheel, and he had a big can, he'd bring us beer in a can, you know, spike it with alcohol. And man, before we'd leave there everybody was high.
Jelly Roll Morton used to call him the can rusher.
Oh, yeah. I can't say this one.

Anyway, they had a little hamburger joint right on the corner of the Spinning Wheel, you know, and we'd get off right about 5:00 o'clock in the morning, man, and I stopped there one night bought some limburger cheese, and -- I mean a hamburger, made a sandwich of it, you understand

what I mean? And I ate an onion on top of it man and went home. My wife asked me, said -- I smoked one of those Italian cigars, they're strong man. And my wife woke me up around 6:00 or 7:00 o'clock in the morning, I said what's the matter she said you too far up in the bed? Now, listen she's smelling that limburger cheese. Oh, man, that was something.
Yeah, that was when everyone was young.
Full of pep, vim and vigor. So you were at the Spinning Wheel for three or four years.
It was back in the thirties, I know. That must have been about --
